BiblicalUsage: Admatha was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat first in the kingdom. He appears once, in the council Ahasuerus calls after Queen Vashti refuses to come before him.
TheologicalSignificance: A courtier's name carries no doctrine, and I won't pretend it does. His value is in the setting: the empire that could summon seven princes over a queen's refusal is the same empire where God was quietly positioning Esther for the saving of His people.
